notes: Primary-record queue for reconstructing the July 28-30 Iran-Jordan-FirstNet escalation sequence. The queue separates observed physical events, official rhetoric, network-service degradation, target intelligence, operational planning, and alliance signaling. It does not establish orchestration, Iranian telecom attribution, staged degradation, forced Jordanian alignment, unlawfulness, or proportionality.

items.record_class: CENTCOM original attempted-surprise-attack statement with native platform metadata, edits, deletion history, and release approval chain
items.activation_effect: Establishes the exact language, publication time, stated launch time, attribution basis, and whether intent characterization was present in the first public object.
items.notes: Preserve the original object rather than relying only on screenshots, media reproductions, or later summaries.

items.record_class: Jordanian Armed Forces interception record and Petra publication metadata
items.activation_effect: Establishes the first Jordanian public wording, publication delay, missile count claimed intercepted, and whether Jordan framed the action as sovereign defense or support of U.S. forces.
items.notes: Seek any earlier briefing, social post, military notice, or embargoed release that predates the indexed Petra item.

items.record_class: IRGC Notice No. 52 in Persian with Sepah News metadata and complete communiqué succession
items.activation_effect: Establishes the authentic Iranian military claim, exact Persian quantity language, described targets, publication time, and whether any battle-damage or retaliation forecast was included.
items.notes: Preserve the Persian primary object and treat English and Arabic versions as later adaptations unless metadata proves otherwise.

items.record_class: Complete missile-launch, trajectory, interceptor, debris, and impact telemetry
items.activation_effect: Determines how many missiles launched, which systems engaged them, whether any malfunctioned or missed, and whether more than one target was assigned.
items.notes: Public statements using multiple, several, and five intercepted must remain distinct until reconciled against telemetry.

items.record_class: U.S. strike-option development, target-validation, authorization, and execution chronology
items.activation_effect: Separates planning that predated the missile launch from option selection, target adjustment, legal review, and executive authorization after the event.
items.notes: The breadth of the operation supports prior preparation but does not identify the actual activation threshold or undisclosed threat inputs.

items.record_class: Presidential remarks, posts, transcripts, and briefing records describing retaliation and escalation
items.activation_effect: Preserves exact punitive language, timing, surrounding questions, and whether the public rationale referenced only the missile launch or a broader threat package.
items.notes: Acquire original video, transcript, and platform object rather than retaining the wire account alone.

items.record_class: AT&T and FirstNet incident telemetry for July 28, including registration, priority, preemption, Band 14, core, tower, backhaul, routing, and restoration records
items.activation_effect: Determines whether a FirstNet primary line experienced a local radio impairment, backhaul failure, core or registration issue, priority-control failure, maintenance event, or unauthorized change.
items.notes: FirstNet priority cannot overcome failed access or transport infrastructure; ordinary congestion must not be assumed without telemetry.

items.record_class: Astound regional network telemetry and customer-contact record for July 28
items.activation_effect: Determines whether severe packet loss, routing impairment, node or CMTS trouble, power, fiber, maintenance, or another upstream condition affected the fixed-broadband path.
items.notes: Preserve the user's inquiry and provider response, including timestamps and any modem-health or packet-loss measurements.

items.record_class: FCC NORS, DIRS, 911, 988, and public-safety communications incident records covering the affected period
items.activation_effect: Establishes whether providers privately reported a qualifying outage or degradation despite limited public disclosure.
items.notes: Public silence and regulatory silence are different claims; seek aggregate or releasable records without assuming a filing exists.

items.record_class: CISA, FBI, NSA, Cyber National Mission Force, and carrier cyber-incident records concerning Iranian access or activity in telecommunications and emergency communications
items.activation_effect: Tests whether the communications degradation had a cyber cause, whether Iranian indicators were present, and whether a classified threat assessment preceded the kinetic response.
items.notes: The July 22 warning establishes threat context only; it does not identify AT&T, FirstNet, Astound, or the July 28 event as victims.

items.record_class: Target-intelligence provenance and Iranian decision record for the Jordan launch
items.activation_effect: Determines what Iran believed was present, the confidence and urgency assigned to the target, the source of that belief, and whether the information was accurate, mistaken, leaked, or deliberately shaped.
items.notes: A believed high-value target can explain a launch even if the target was absent; orchestration requires evidence that the belief environment was deliberately shaped.

items.record_class: U.S.-Jordan communications, talking points, embargoes, and statement-approval chronology
items.activation_effect: Distinguishes unilateral rapid U.S. publication from coordinated messaging, requested delay, embargo, persuasion, or coercion affecting Jordan's later statement.
items.notes: Washington could exploit predictable Jordanian disclosure latency without ordering the delay; direct coordination remains a separate claim requiring records.
